QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_6

question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (Cat III AIF) is formalising documentation for a structured private-investment block trade. Which of the following are the TWO principal 'definitive agreements' described in Chapter 11 for AIF investments?

answer.text: Prime Brokerage Agreement and Custody Agreement
Investor Charter and Code of Conduct
ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex
Share Subscription/Purchase Agreement and Shareholders' Agreement

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 11 identifies the two main 'definitive agreements' as: (1) Share Subscription/Purchase Agreement — between AIF and investee company, the main transaction document for equity financing; (2) Shareholders' Agreement — inter-se among existing shareholders and the AIF, binding shareholders to agreed rights/obligations. The Trap: Some options list service-provider contracts (operational, not transactional). Governance documents are not transaction closers. ISDA/CSA is derivatives documentation — important for Cat III trading, but NOT 'definitive agreements' as the chapter defines for investee-company investments. Cross-Exam Context: Same taxonomy in XIX-C/D. Distinguish from PB/ISDA stack which is specific to Cat III hedge-fund trading infrastructure (relevant but categorically different). Manager's Pro-Tip: Even for a Cat III special-situations primary allotment, always ensure the Shareholders' Agreement gets amended into the investee's AoA — otherwise your preferential rights (anti-dilution, liquidation preference, tag/drag) may be unenforceable against new shareholders.
